- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment, leading to delayed or exaggerated price corrections; apply lagged smoothing to dampen immediate reactions.
- In 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts mid-to-late period prices after initial spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome in such cases.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add 1–2 day lagged correction buffer for such scenarios.
